newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Campaigning reopens for Madagascar presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Campaigning reopens for Madagascar presidential poll.

text.p: Campaigning for Madagascar's presidential election reopened quietly on Sunday -- with the field for the second round of voting, scheduled for December 29, limited to the country's last two presidents.

Local newspapers reported retired admiral Didier Ratsiraka, 60, who ruled from 1975 to 1993, is the favourite to win against medical professor Albert Zafy, 69, who succeeded Ratsiraka after two years of unprecedented political protest.
The election was ordered after Zafy was impeached by his own parliament last July for contravening the constitution and abusing his presidential powers.
The two former presidents led the first round of voting early in November, when 15 rival candidates contested the poll. Ratsiraka got 36.61 per cent of the vote, against Zafy's 23.39 per cent.

Ratsiraka, who returned from 18 months of voluntary exile in France to contest the election, has been accorded an enthusiastic welcome from the people -- in sharp contrast to the widespread demands for his removal in 1993.
Political observers said the wave of support for Ratsiraka reflected discontent with Zafy's performance as president.
Ratsiraka has promised to seek approval for constitutional changes once he is elected.
Campaigning for the second-round poll began on a low note on Sunday, but was expected to gather pace in the next two weeks.

Observers said Ratsiraka's chances were greatly improved when millionaire businessman Herizo Razafimahaleo, who secured 15.13 per cent of the first-round votes, announced his support for Ratsiraka last week.
